acceptance_checks: With a fake gh whose protection API fails on run 1, run 2 re-attempts both the protection and workflow-permissions calls (today both are zero).
Same with the runtime token unset on run 1: run 2 attempts the secret set.
Run 2 still exits non-zero when the underlying cause is unfixed.
shiki init against an existing repo whose default branch holds a different commit leaves that branch unchanged and either succeeds or exits with a ShikiError; the reflog contains no reset.
install-target --force over a target with its own guardian policy preserves that value and warns that it was preserved.
doctor --online against a not-protected stub emits fail and exit 1; the 403 stub still emits warn.
doctor does not fail on a sibling git worktree that carries no Shiki task record; a genuinely orphaned task worktree is still reported.
non_goals: Changing the branch-protection payload or required-check derivation

findings.detail: git diff main...HEAD includes intervening merged goals' mirror records and code (mergegate_check.py, shiki_runtime.py, schemas, many .shiki records) because this worktree was cut from a stale local main. This is the exact bug class fixed for future worktrees by the sibling task T-...9ee6b8e0, not a defect in these changes. MergeGate derives its base from origin/main, so the real PR diff is the 8 task-locked files; this is a rebase concern, identical to the recorded PR #187 finding. Non-blocking.
findings.title: PR diff carries large foreign .shiki mirror state (stale-local-main base)

scope: In scripts/shiki_bootstrap.py make cmd_start call initialize_target_from_start unconditionally when execution is confirmed, so a retry after a failed first run re-attempts secret, branch protection and workflow permissions instead of silently skipping all GitHub governance setup; and use plain git checkout when the branch already exists, raising ShikiError on failure instead of forcing the ref with -B. In scripts/shiki_installer.py treat guardian-policy.json, config.yaml and migrations/state.json as create-if-absent even under --force, warning that they were preserved. In scripts/shiki_doctor.py distinguish 404 / not-protected (fail) from 403 (warn). Also correct doctor's unregistered-worktree check: it currently fails on any sibling git worktree lacking a .shiki/worktrees record, which includes the coordinator's own session worktree as seen from inside every dispatched task worktree (they share one gitdir). That makes a doctor-dependent test red in every dispatch for a reason no implementer can fix inside its locks. Report a worktree that carries no Shiki task as informational, not as a failure.
test_command: bash scripts/test_shiki_start.sh && bash scripts/test_shiki_init.sh && bash scripts/test_shiki_doctor.sh && bash scripts/test_shiki_p2_branch_protection_failure.sh && python3 -m unittest discover -s tests
title: Never destroy an existing target, never silently skip its governance setup
